name: TrafficEye
title: Traffic violation detection that leaves the final call to an officer
role: Solo build: models, backend and control-room UI
summary: Detects riders without helmets, red-light jumping and triple riding from a camera, video or photo, reads number plates, and saves evidence that an officer reviews before a printable e-challan is issued.

metrics.label: violation types: no helmet, red-light jump, triple riding
models: YOLO11s road users, YOLO26-L helmets, open-lpr plates
frames of the same tracked bike before a helmet or triple-riding ticket
minimum vehicle width before its plate is read

problem: Manual enforcement catches a small share of helmet, red-light and overloading offences, and handwritten tickets are hard to back up with evidence.
A system that issues fines on its own is only as good as its worst false positive. A wrong ticket for a law-abiding rider costs more than a missed one, so every detection has to be reviewable.

constraints.label: CPU only
constraints.text: It runs without a GPU, so each frame gets at most 2 plate reads and helmet checks on at most 6 motorcyclists, largest first.

constraints.label: Fixed camera
constraints.text: Red-light detection needs a stop line drawn once per camera; a single photo can't show a vehicle crossing it.

constraints.label: Distance
constraints.text: Riders under 60 px tall are too far away to judge, and small plates are enlarged 2× before reading.

constraints.label: Safe models
constraints.text: The helmet model is loaded as ONNX on purpose: unlike a .pt file, it can't run code when it's loaded.

architecture.caption: YOLO11s finds road users and traffic lights. Bikes are joined with their riders and checked by a traffic helmet model, IoU tracks feed per-vehicle violation rules, and open-lpr reads plates for evidence.

sections.heading: Red-light jumping without tickets for cars waiting at the line
paras: A vehicle's front (the bottom-centre of its box) is tracked against the camera's stop line, using signed distance and the approach direction. A ticket needs the vehicle to be clearly before the line, then clearly past it, within the line's span, while the signal is red.

Vehicles waiting on the line jitter across it by a pixel or two, so I added hysteresis: a side only counts once the vehicle is past it by 2% of the frame or 15% of its own height. Boxes cut off by the frame edge are ignored, and each vehicle can be ticketed once per violation type.

sections.heading: Reading the signal colour from pixels
paras: The light's state comes from counting bright, saturated pixels in the red, green and yellow hue bands of its box. A lit lamp covers a few percent of the head; less than 1.5% is treated as reflection.

Many signal heads are painted yellow, so a box that's more than 25% amber is treated as housing, not a lit lamp. The result is a majority vote over the last 3 readings, so one blurry frame can't flip red to green, and an operator can override it by hand.

challenges.title: Construction hard-hat models failed on motorcyclists
challenges.text: The helmet models I had from SiteSentinel were trained on building sites, not traffic. I compared three models on 2,190 traffic photos and chose a YOLO26-L traffic helmet model at confidence 0.5 because it produced the fewest wrong tickets. Every detection still waits in a review queue.

challenges.title: Plates unreadable at the moment of the violation
challenges.text: Every vehicle's plate is read from 80 px wide onwards and re-read as it gets closer, keeping the best read until one reaches 0.85 confidence. A violation reuses that earlier read, falls back to OCR on the helmet model's plate box, or is recorded as NOT READ for the officer to type in.

challenges.title: Counting riders on a bike
challenges.text: A person counts as a rider when the lower half of their box overlaps the motorcycle by at least 30%, confirmed by heads from the helmet model, so a pedestrian standing beside the bike isn't counted towards triple riding.

outcome: TrafficEye takes a webcam, uploaded video (sampled at 5 frames per second) or photos, tracks vehicles, and records each violation with an annotated, time-stamped frame, a close-up and a plate crop.

Officers work through a review queue, correct the plate if needed and issue a printable e-challan or reject the detection. Payments are tracked, and an Offenders view groups violations by plate to show repeat offenders and unpaid fines.
